Reference

  • Integrations

Using WhatEverFi

Routines

A routine is a prompt a bot runs on its own: on a schedule, when something changes, or when another service calls it.

Ask for one in chat

The quickest way is to ask:

  • “Every weekday at 8am, summarize my inbox.”
  • “Remind me in 20 minutes to call Dana.”
  • “Every Monday, check our competitors’ pricing pages and tell me what changed.”

The bot creates the routine and reports each run back in the same chat.

Create or edit one yourself

Open the bot’s computer with Agent computer at the top of the chat. Below the screen is the bot’s Routines list. Choose Create Routine (the +), or click a routine to edit it.

  1. Name the routine and write the Instruction: what it should do each time it runs.
  2. Under When to run, choose Add trigger.
  3. Choose Save.

Under Advanced you can give a routine its own Model and Thinking level, for example a cheaper model for a simple daily check.

Triggers

On a schedule

Every hour, every day, weekdays, every week, every month, or a custom interval. Advanced… accepts a cron expression. Times use your timezone, set in Settings → General.

When something changes

The bot checks something at a set interval (Check every, from 5 minutes to a day) and runs only when it changed. What to watch can be files or folders on the computer, a command’s output, or a tool from a connected app. Turn on Post “No changes” in chat if you want a note every time. A watch can’t be combined with a schedule.

Webhook

Gives you a URL and key. Any service that can send a POST request can start the routine.

Git event

Gives you a URL to add as a GitHub webhook, so pushes, issues and pull requests can start the routine.

Email

Runs when mail arrives at the bot’s own address, such as scout@bots.example.com. The first time, pick the part before the @; it stays the bot’s for good. Forward or CC mail to it and the routine runs with that email. Choose who can start it: Only me, or Anyone at your own email domain. Mail from anyone else, and mail sent BCC, starts nothing, but the bot keeps every email in its inbox either way. If mail from your own address can’t be verified, the chat says so; your email provider then needs DKIM signing turned on for your domain. Appears only when your server receives email.

Slack message

Runs when the bot receives a message in Slack. Needs Slack connected.

A routine run started by a webhook, an email or a Slack message follows your approval mode and Always allow list. Since outside text could steer it, tools that change something are checked even if they never ask in your own chats, and a purchase is refused. Always allow on a tool such as shell or the browser lets outside text use it freely.

Test, pause and review

  • Test run runs a saved routine now.
  • Turn off Active to pause a routine without deleting it.
  • Run history shows each past run and its result.
  • A running routine shows Running in the list, with Stop.

On mobile

The mobile app lists a bot’s routines from its profile. Tap + to create one. Tapping a routine shows its instruction, schedule, next run and run history, with a switch to pause it and a button to test it; Edit routine changes its name, instruction and schedules, or deletes it. Webhook, Git event, Slack message and change triggers, and a routine’s own model, are set up in chat or the web or desktop app; mobile shows them and keeps them as they are.
